name: Hrdle
summary: Web-based terminal session manager for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Kimi). Runs them in herdr workspaces and provides a web UI for remote access from tablets and phones

stack.transport: Multiplexed WebSocket /ws/mux + the herdr socket API (NDJSON RPC) + per-pane control streams. The terminal is drawn server-side: PaneViewport frames composed from pane.read (herdr holds the history, up to 1000 lines)

workspaces.name: backend
workspaces.desc: Hono API server (Bun). Drives herdr, serves history and peers, and provides the CLI

workspaces.name: frontend
workspaces.desc: React SPA. Three layouts: tablet, mobile and desktop

workspaces.name: glasses
workspaces.desc: The EVEN G2 glasses app (EvenHub SDK -> out.ehpk). Its types are duplicated by hand, so a WS protocol change has to be followed here

diagram: | Hono API server  | <-----------> | herdr | <----> | Claude Code / Codex |
| Peer Hrdle x N   |  Tailscale tailnet (auto-discovery)

services.name: HerdrClient
services.summary: Low-level client for the herdr socket API. NDJSON RPC (one connection per request; only events.subscribe is held open), a UTF-8-safe line reader built on a streaming TextDecoder, pane id conversion (%N <-> wK:pN), and PaneController (a resident control stream: raw input as base64, terminal.resize, terminal.frame)

services.name: HerdrControlSession
services.summary: One instance per session (= one herdr workspace). Owns the split tree, tracks focus, spawns lazy controllers (WS subscribe or first input only; read-only REST stays pure RPC), tracks the cursor and alt-screen state by scanning frames, and gives a client a 30s grace period. captureViewportHerdr composes the viewport (the visible slice, then recent, capped at 1000 lines). A pane with no runtime yet returns no scroll, which is a normal transient state right after a restore rather than a reason to refuse: it falls back to the client's rows and continues the subscribe, because refusing deadlocks against herdr's resume (which waits for a client size) and the session never opens (#407)

services.name: HerdrAgentStatusWatcher
services.summary: Subscribes to herdr's pane.agent_status_changed (a per-pane subscription that requires pane_id) and to pane lifecycle events, pushing the session list the moment an agent's state changes. The values come from pane.list, so a dropped event costs latency rather than correctness (#390)

services.name: HerdrLayout
services.summary: The split tree this app owns (herdr's grid cannot be resized headlessly). Split, close, zoom, ratio adjustment and absolute sizing, rendered to tmux-convention TmuxLayoutNode rectangles

services.name: HerdrService
services.summary: Maps session-level operations onto herdr workspaces: listing (agent detection from pane.process_info, native session ids from agent.list, agent_status: idle/working/blocked/done), create and kill, and previews

services.name: HerdrUpdateService
services.summary: Detects version skew between the herdr binary and the running server (herdr update swaps the binary and leaves the server on the old build). Reads herdr status --json with a 30s cache and warns on the dashboard. Applying it (update plus a supervised restart) happens only through POST /api/herdr/apply-update as a user action, never from the auto-update path. Output it cannot interpret degrades to no warning (#393)

services.name: PaneState
services.summary: The stripAnsi / detectPaneState heuristics (pane state for `send --wait` and `peek`)

services.name: ClaudeCodeService
services.summary: Watches Claude Code session state through the .jsonl files under ~/.claude/projects. Layered caches (TTY 10s, session data 30s, path resolution 3s, each capped at 1000 entries). Parses the JSONL to detect a permission prompt, tool use and the waiting-for-input state

services.name: SessionHistoryService
services.summary: Serves past session history and conversations from the JSONL under ~/.claude/projects. Scans projects in parallel, extracts firstPrompt / lastPrompt / git branch / token usage / recap, and implements streaming full-text search (SSE)

services.name: SessionMetadataService
services.summary: Persists a session's theme, title and display order in herdr-session-metadata.json, with herdr-last-known-sessions.json kept separately for recovery after a restart (the file names keep it apart from the tmux-era store)

services.name: SessionsService
services.summary: File-based CRUD for session metadata (id, name, createdAt, lastAccessedAt, state), sorted by lastAccessedAt descending

services.name: PromptHistoryService
services.summary: Substring search over ~/.claude/history.jsonl (case-insensitive), returning matches newest first with their project path and session ID

services.name: FileService
services.summary: Safe file and directory operations with path traversal prevention. Decides binary from the extension plus a heuristic (NUL bytes, the ratio of control characters) and returns UTF-8 or base64

services.name: FileChangeTracker
services.summary: Extracts Write/Edit tool use (path, old/new string, timestamp) from the Claude Code JSONL. Deduplicates per path and sorts chronologically for the change-history UI

services.name: AnthropicUsageService
services.summary: Fetches usage limits (the 5-hour and 7-day cycles) from the Anthropic API. The attempt is stamped when it starts and gated on a 60s TTL, so upstream sees at most one call a minute regardless of whether the last one succeeded, failed or threw (the rate limit is per account, making this the only thing standing between polling and a 429). A 429 backs off for longer, honoring Retry-After, and in-flight requests are coalesced. Also estimates when the current pace reaches the limit. Extracts per-model limits (Fable and friends) from the scoped entries in `limits[]` - the overall cycle can look comfortable while a model-specific one is pinned. Entries it cannot interpret are discarded rather than guessed at

services.name: AnthropicModels
services.summary: Fetches Anthropic model metadata (maximum input tokens and so on). 24h cache with request coalescing. Used by the cost and usage calculations

services.name: StatsService
services.summary: Reads ~/.claude/stats-cache.json (written by the Claude CLI) and aggregates daily activity and per-model token kinds (input/cache_read/cache_creation/output). Estimates cost from a fixed price table

services.name: UsageHistoryService
services.summary: Records usage snapshots to /tmp/hrdle-usage-history.json, throttled to 30s. Keeps 8 days for the utilization trend chart. Per-model limits are recorded under `scoped` (an older snapshot without that key counts as 'not measured' rather than 0%)

services.name: SystemMetricsService
services.summary: Collects CPU%, memory, swap and load average. A rolling history of 60 entries (minimum 3s between snapshots). Swap comes from /proc/meminfo (Linux only)

services.name: SessionMetricsService
services.summary: Aggregates per-session context tokens (the last turn's input + cache_creation + cache_read) and totals from the JSONL, cached on mtime+size. Process-tree RSS comes from ps (1s cache)

services.name: CodexService
services.summary: Reads an active thread's metadata (title, tokens_used, git_branch, cwd) from Codex's SQLite threads table (state_5.sqlite), cached 5s by cwd. Token usage is extracted from the tail of the rollout file (up to 4MB)

services.name: CodexConversationService
services.summary: Converts Codex rollout JSONL events (user_message, agent_message, function_call and so on) into Claude-shaped ConversationMessages. The rollout path is resolved from the SQLite threads table

services.name: CodexHistoryService
services.summary: Scans the date-partitioned tree under ~/.codex/sessions (YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl) with a per-file mtime cache, groups by cwd and merges the result into the Claude Code history

services.name: CodexUsageService
services.summary: Takes rate_limits events from up to the 8 most recent rollouts and builds the 5h/7d cycles' utilization, reset times and limit-hit estimates. 30s cache

services.name: ConversationWatcher
services.summary: Watches the Claude Code / Codex JSONL with fs.watch plus a 150ms debounce and notifies WebSocket subscribers of new turns only. Tracks mtime to avoid redundant parsing

services.name: HookStatusService
services.summary: Reports whether the hooks this app still needs are configured (Stop for the notification body, PostToolUse/AskUserQuestion for the question's tool name). The indicator's state transitions come from herdr, so PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit are unnecessary (#390)

services.name: AuthService
services.summary: Server-password authentication, and issuing and verifying JWT session tokens

services.name: PeerRegistry
services.summary: Persists peers.json through an atomic rename plus a module-level mutation lock (serializing load-mutate-save). Manages wsToken, lastSeenAt and error records, round-robin color palette assignment, and cross-peer session order

services.name: PeerAuth
services.summary: Logs in to a peer on the user's behalf (POST /api/auth/login, 5s timeout). Stores the JWT for later API and WS calls and records a 401 as unauthorized. Connectivity is checked through /health

services.name: PeerDiscovery
services.summary: Lists the tailnet's online peers through `tailscale status --json` and probes each :5923/health in parallel with a 3s timeout. A peer running the app comes back as a DiscoveredPeer with its version

services.name: PeerUrl
services.summary: SSRF guard for peer URLs (#235). Rejects anything that is not https, plus loopback, link-local, RFC1918 and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and allows only Tailscale hosts (*.ts.net, CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, ULA fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48)

hooks.name: useMultiplexedTerminal
hooks.summary: A shared singleton WebSocket to /ws/mux: auto-reconnect, keepalive pings, per-session subscription, base64 I/O and viewport dispatch. Returns the operations (sendInput, resize, splitPane, requestViewport and the rest). A peerWsBase connects it to a remote peer instead

hooks.name: useSessions
hooks.summary: State for the active sessions. Aggregates several peers through usePeerSessionsWatcher over a shared module-level cache. Provides createSession, deleteSession and updateSessionTheme

hooks.name: useSessionHistory
hooks.summary: History browsing: fetching projects across peers, managing the projectKey (peerId::dirName), SSE streaming search (with the Bearer token attached), resumeSession and fetchConversation

hooks.name: useFlatHistoryItems
hooks.summary: Flattens the project-grouped history into History V2's filterable list. Hydrates four at a time and sorts by modification time descending

hooks.name: useHistoryActions
hooks.summary: The shared logic for resuming, navigating and showing a conversation from history (used by both the V1 and V2 views)

hooks.name: useHistoryV2Flag
hooks.summary: History V2's feature flag. localStorage `hrdle-history-v2` (older prefixes still read) (on by default), watching the storage event

hooks.name: useDashboard
hooks.summary: Polls /api/dashboard (every 60s) and returns the DashboardResponse

hooks.name: useFileViewer
hooks.summary: File viewer state: listDirectory, readFile, getChanges, getGitChanges, getGitDiff. An optional peerId fetches a remote peer's files

hooks.name: useViewHistory
hooks.summary: Back navigation for the file viewer (the browser/file/changes/diff view modes). An in-memory stack synchronized with window.history

hooks.name: useViewerSettings
hooks.summary: Viewer settings. Word wrap (per file) and font size (global, 8-32px) persisted in localStorage

hooks.name: useAuth
hooks.summary: Authentication state. Persists the token in localStorage and provides login and logout

hooks.name: useAuthBlobUrl
hooks.summary: Fetches a resource with the auth header and exposes it as a blob URL (for the src of an img, video or iframe). Revokes it automatically

hooks.name: useTheme
hooks.summary: Dark and light theme switching (localStorage)

hooks.name: useUiScale
hooks.summary: Persists the UI scale factor and applies it to the CSS variable (localStorage)

hooks.name: useNetworkLatency
hooks.summary: Measures WebSocket and API latency (a /health ping every 30s, subscribing to the latency store)

hooks.name: useLineSelection
hooks.summary: Line-range selection utilities for the file viewer

hooks.name: useSelectionMode
hooks.summary: The touch-selection state machine behind SelectionOverlay (start and end cells, drag handles, copying to the clipboard)

hooks.name: useInputEcho
hooks.summary: Echoes what is typed into the InputBar back into the conversation or chat view while the terminal is hidden. Arrows, Ctrl and other special keys are shown as symbols

hooks.name: useConversationStream
hooks.summary: Subscribes to the /ws/mux conversation stream (subscribe-conversation) and exposes the incremental conversation-update messages

hooks.name: useAgentConversation
hooks.summary: A unified hook that picks the conversation source by the active session's agent: Claude over the WebSocket stream, Codex by polling

hooks.name: useCodexConversation
hooks.summary: The polling loader for a Codex conversation (every 5s, transcript plus token usage)

hooks.name: usePeers
hooks.summary: CRUD and state for the peer list (5s polling, a module-level cache with broadcast). addPeer, updatePeer, deletePeer, verifyPeer, reorderPeers

hooks.name: usePeerConnection
hooks.summary: Derives the connection info (wsBase, apiBase, token) from a session's peerId. A remote peer is converted from peer.url

hooks.name: usePeerSessionsWatcher
hooks.summary: Holds a persistent /ws/mux WebSocket per remote peer, so sessions-updated pushes and hook-events arrive without polling. Reconnects automatically

hooks.name: usePeerServerMetrics
hooks.summary: Polls a peer's dashboard metrics (systemMetrics, diskUsage, connectedClients) every 30s

hooks.name: usePinchZoom
hooks.summary: Two-finger pinch zoom gesture handling. Clamped to min/max, with the transient (onChange) and persistent (onCommit) paths separated

hooks.name: useScrollRatio
hooks.summary: Tracks and restores a scrollable element's position ratio (0..1)

websocket.description: One multiplexed WebSocket. The client subscribes per session, and the terminal is delivered as PaneViewport frames (offset-based, server-side scrollback). Besides answering request-viewport, a live subscriber (offset=0) also receives unsolicited pushes when a herdr frame arrives. Every client frame is validated with zod (#231)
websocket.binary_format: Unused (every frame is JSON text; pane output rides along in viewport.lines as ANSI-encoded strings)

types.name: SessionResponse

types.name: ExtendedSessionResponse
types.fields: extends SessionResponse + indicatorState, ccSessionId, agentSessionId, currentCommand, ccSummary, ccFirstPrompt, ccRecap, waitingToolName, panes, messageCount, gitBranch, durationMinutes, metrics, peerId

types.name: PaneInfo

types.name: TmuxLayoutNode
types.fields: type ('leaf' | 'horizontal' | 'vertical'), width, height, x, y, paneId?, children?

types.name: PaneViewport
types.fields: paneId, cols, rows, lines (exactly rows lines, ANSI-encoded), cursor (PaneCursor), modes (PaneModes), historySize, offset (0 = the live edge), atTail

types.name: PaneCursor
types.fields: x, y (0-based), visible (false when offset>0)

types.name: PaneModes
types.fields: altScreen (whether this is an alternate screen, as vim or htop use)

types.name: ControlClientMessage
types.fields: input | resize | split | close-pane | resize-pane | select-pane | adjust-pane | equalize-panes | zoom-pane | respawn-pane | request-viewport | ping | client-info

types.name: ControlServerMessage
types.fields: layout | viewport | ready | pong | error | pane-dead | hook-event

types.name: MuxClientMessage
types.fields: subscribe | unsubscribe | subscribe-conversation | unsubscribe-conversation | (ControlClientMessage + sessionId)

types.name: MuxServerMessage
types.fields: subscribed | unsubscribed | sessions-updated | conversation-* | initial-conversation | (ControlServerMessage + sessionId)

types.name: Peer
types.fields: id ('local' | 'p_xxxx'), nickname, url ('self' | https URL), color, order

types.name: PeerClientView
types.fields: extends Peer + wsToken (the Bearer for a WS straight to the peer), status, lastSeenAt, latencyMs, errorMessage

types.name: DiscoveredPeer
types.fields: What Tailscale discovery found: host, url, version, alreadyRegistered

types.name: HistorySession
types.fields: sessionId, projectPath, projectName, firstPrompt (an old name; it actually holds the last user message), lastPrompt, recap, recapAt, modified, messageCount, gitBranch, agent, peerId

types.name: SessionMetrics
types.fields: contextTokens, contextMaxTokens, contextPercent, totalInputTokens, totalCacheCreationTokens, totalCacheReadTokens, totalOutputTokens, totalTokens, memoryRssBytes

types.name: DashboardResponse
types.fields: usageLimits, usageLimitsStatus, codexUsageLimits, usageHistory, dailyActivity, modelUsage, costEstimates, hourlyActivity, version, systemMetrics, diskUsage, connectedClients

types.name: ConversationMessage
types.fields: role, content, timestamp, thinking, toolUse, toolResult

types.name: UsageLimits
types.fields: fiveHour (UsageCycleInfo), sevenDay (UsageCycleInfo)

types.name: SessionState
types.fields: 'idle' | 'working' | 'waiting_input' | 'waiting_permission' | 'disconnected' | 'lost'

types.name: IndicatorState
types.fields: 'processing' | 'waiting_input' | 'idle' | 'completed'

types.name: AgentProvider
types.fields: 'claude' | 'codex' (the AGENT_PROVIDERS registry defines the resume command and the rest)

data_flows.name: Terminal input
steps: The browser (xterm onData / InputBar)
useMultiplexedTerminal.sendInput → JSON { type:'input', sessionId, paneId, data: base64 }
Validated with zod in /ws/mux (terminal-mux.ts)
HerdrControlSession.sendInput (raw bytes as base64 into the control stream)
The herdr pane's PTY -> the Claude Code / Codex process

data_flows.name: Terminal output (viewport)
steps: herdr terminal.frame (pane control stream)
HerdrControlSession sees the output (a frame arrives)
PaneViewport captures the visible region (padFill unless it is an alt screen)
The viewport frame { paneId, lines, cursor, modes, historySize, offset, atTail } is pushed to live subscribers
Frontend: viewportToVTSequence() turns it into a VT sequence
xterm.js term.write() updates the screen (render-only, scrollback:0)

data_flows.name: Reading the scrollback
steps: The user scrolls (wheel or touch)
Sends request-viewport { paneId, offset: N }
The server reads the viewport N lines up
Replies with a viewport (atTail=false, the cursor hidden)
Tapping the terminal or showing the soft keyboard returns to offset=0 (live)

data_flows.name: Layout synchronization
steps: A pane operation (split / close / resize / zoom)
A split or resize, or a pane event, triggers a reconcile
HerdrLayout converts the split tree into TmuxLayoutNode rectangles
The layout frame goes to every subscribed client
PaneContainer redraws the tree and Terminal.setExactSize() fixes the size

data_flows.name: Hook notifications
steps: A Claude Code / Codex hook (Stop, PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse)
The notify command (reading the hook JSON from stdin)
POST /api/notify (unauthenticated)
HookStatusService updates the session's indicator state
The hook-event frame is broadcast over the WebSocket (debounced to one notification)
An OS notification through the browser Notification API

data_flows.name: The real-time conversation stream
steps: The client sends subscribe-conversation { sessionId }
ConversationWatcher watches that JSONL with fs.watch (150ms debounce)
initial-conversation carries the whole thing; conversation-update then carries new turns only
ChatView / ConversationViewer render the increment

data_flows.name: Aggregating peer sessions
steps: A peer is registered in PeerManager (PeerAuth logs in and stores the JWT; PeerUrl guards against SSRF)
usePeers polls /api/peers every 5s (the list and its status)
usePeerSessionsWatcher holds a WS to each remote peer's /ws/mux with its wsToken
Each peer's sessions-updated and hook-event arrive
useSessions merges the local and peer sessions for the UI

data_flows.name: Remote pane control (`send` / `peek`)
steps: CLI: hrdle send <peer>:<session>:<paneId> [text]
Resolves the peer (local / peer id / nickname) and its credentials
POST /api/sessions/:id/panes/input (with --wait it captures a viewport afterwards)
GET /api/sessions/:id/panes/:paneId/viewport (hrdle peek)
Prints the viewport's last N lines and the detected state (idle / processing / permission_prompt / ask_user_question)
